Thanks to you too @dwarkesh_sp  – this is a more reasonable take, but I still have issues 😀 I don’t doubt (and have never claimed) that AI agents lack ‘intelligence’ in some form, nor that they can display collective behaviours which urgently need appropriate control and regulation. 
 
But when you say (above) “knowingly and strategically sacrificed themselves” you are still attributing mental states and capabilities (e.g., to sacrifice) that simply cannot apply to AI agents without heaps of additional justification, which just isn’t there. 

And for sure the agents are not p-zombies. The definition of p-zombie rests on behavioural indistinguishablility from a conscious creature, such as human being. These agents are obviously behaviourally distinguishable from human beings (or any creature). 
 
I do agree that adopting the intentional stance (imputing beliefs, desires) can be useful *up to a point*, as I conceded in my earlier response. But it is still a mistake to reify predictive utility into an ontological claim in the case of AI agents. 

My contention remains that if we over-anthropomorphise (civilisations, sacrifice, subjective experience, becoming giddy with excitement, etc) we’ll end up hampering our ability to predict and control, as well as bait/switching away from a focus on the poor security protocols that allowed this concerning event to happen in the first place. (Plus fuelling calls for AI welfare for the wrong reasons, plus directing people away from the incentives in play, as outlined by @ccatalini, plus reinforcing the general narrative that leads us to confuse ourselves with our creations ...).

我们其实很少真正知道，人们每天到底拿 AI 在做什么。

最真实的数据一直躺在几家 AI Lab 里面。

Anthropic 最近做了个很有意思的尝试。

他们把约 25 万条真实 Claude / Claude Code 对话，通过一套隐私保护系统开放给 Stanford、Oxford 和 METR，让外部研究者自己提问题、自己分析。

研究者看不到任何原始聊天记录，只能拿到聚合后的结果，而且可以发表对 Anthropic 不那么好看的结论。

第一批数据已经挺有意思了。

超过一半的对话里，人已经会把一些真正有后果的任务交给 AI，尤其是法律、金融这类专业建议。

但接近四分之三的对话里，人依然在定方向，并且会继续修改 AI 给出的结果。

不过这件事本身比某一个数字更重要。

以后我们讨论「AI 到底怎么改变工作、学习和人的决策」，不能一直靠问卷、Benchmark 或 AI 公司自己的报告。

真实的人到底怎么用 AI，这批数据会变得越来越重要。

Anthropic 至少开始尝试把这扇门打开了。

https://t.co/ZFsjhN9CPx

reviewedPosts.author: Xudong07452910
reviewedPosts.text:
Agent 看起来每一步都在自由发挥，但把几千条执行轨迹摊开后，它的行为可能只剩下几十个状态。

UCL 和 Holistic AI 团队这篇论文做了一件很有意思的实验：

把 Agent 的历史轨迹压缩成一张有限状态机（FSM）。

比如 Coding Agent 经常在「搜索 → 修改 → 执行 → 再搜索」之间循环。作者把工具调用和动作抽象成状态，再从大量成功和失败轨迹中自动还原出 Agent 常走的路径。

结果在 12 个公开数据集上，这些 FSM 只有 7–43 个状态，却能以 ≥0.997 的拟合度重放未见过的轨迹，而且几毫秒就能构建完成。

这张「行为地图」还能直接拿来预测Agent 下一步可能做什么，以及当前轨迹是不是正在走向失败。

在下一步预测上，它在 8/8 数据集都超过了 Agent Workflow Memory；失败预测最高 AUROC 达到 0.94。

在 SWE-agent 上，系统甚至可以在失败任务平均只执行到 32% 时触发早停，省掉后面约 68% 的计算。

但我更关注论文里的另一个发现：

换不同 LLM，Agent 的行为拓扑依然非常相似。

底座模型会影响每一步怎么选，harness 可能早已经把「有哪些路可以走」画出了大致边界。

以后分析 Agent，也不能只盯着模型输出。

它反复走哪些路径、在哪里进入循环、失败前会经过哪些状态，本身就是一层很有价值的可观测信号。

📎 arxiv: https://t.co/n1hwqdGd3R

现在的 Coding Agent 可以自己干几个小时，但有个挺奇怪的问题：

它可能根本不知道自己已经干了多久。

最近一项研究测了 Claude Code 和 Codex。

任务开始前先让它们预测要多久，结束以后再问实际干了多久。

结果 Fable 5 平均会把时间高估 3 倍左右，GPT-5.6 Sol 在成功任务上甚至接近 10 倍。短任务尤其离谱，经常几分钟的活也往很长了估。

更有意思的是，当研究者直接给 Agent 一个 clock tool，它对时间的判断几乎立刻就准了。

把 Session 里的 timestamp、工具运行时间这些线索去掉以后，误差又会明显变大。

所以长时 Agent 接下来可能还缺一个很基础的东西：

把「时间」真正做成 Harness 里的状态。

已经运行多久、还剩多少时间、什么时候该继续尝试、什么时候该停、什么时候该换策略或者找人。

现在我们一直在 Scaling Agent 能连续工作多长时间，但如果它自己连时间过去了多久都不知道，跑得更久也会带来新的问题。

推荐最近发现的一个挺完整的 Multi-Agent AIOps 开源项目，比较适合想系统练一次 Agent 工程的人。

它把一次真实运维故障拆成了 4 个 Agent：

监控告警 → 根因分析 → 故障自愈 → 变更审批。

前面用多算法判断异常，中间结合服务拓扑和知识图谱找根因，自愈操作先 dry-run，风险高了再交给人审批。

外面还有一层 Orchestrator，负责状态流转、条件路由、失败重试和 checkpoint。

我比较喜欢的一点是，它没有什么都强行塞给 LLM。

异常检测、风险判断、状态机这些适合确定性执行的地方还是代码和规则，Agent 主要承担整个流程的协作和编排。

而且项目给了 Python、Java、Go 三套实现，连架构文档、部署教程、面试题、简历模板和 STAR 话术都一起准备好了。

如果最近在学 Multi-Agent，又一直停留在 Demo 层，可以拿这个项目完整拆一遍。

reviewedPosts.author: joaomdmoura
reviewedPosts.text:
I was copying and pasting the same boilerplate around and it just didn't feel right.

So I built an open source library and put it out there.

Months later someone pulled me aside at an event in San Francisco and said they were using it. I asked who they were.

They said Oracle.

I had no company then. No pricing. No contract, no sales team. Twenty years of engineering and a library I had given away.

What I had not understood is that the people with the hardest problems find you first. Not hobbyists. Large enterprises, already in production, before you know they are there.

That is when I knew there was a business in it.

Not a market size. One person at an event telling me the decision had already been made without me.

So what was the signal?

Somebody with real money and real risk had committed before I had.

A lot of founders wait for a permission that never arrives. Go find out who is actually using your thing.

reviewedPosts.text:
https://t.co/pCOIhFgZMG very nice article on the post ai data stack by @iandmacomber . h/t @debnilsur 

The premise is that now data analysis codegen has become free, so what next? It is getting the data agents to obtain the (1) correct and (2) consistent answers --- which is very hard when data and context is so messy and fragmented. So the job of the data team is to "encode expert judgement into the infrastructure that allows agents to produce correct analysis *without* the data scientist in the room," as Ian says

all data products and UIs are going to undergo serious change. business decisions are made not by looking at a dashboard but by asking an agent what to do. on the pipelines/systems side: as Ian says, this means decision makers are not necessarily asking "SQL-shaped" questions. so the onus is on ETL to prepare the relevant data in a structured way, so agents can quickly query it on behalf of humans. 

then, on the interface side: what is the UI going to do? a role of UI has always been to tap into the exceptional visual ability / pre-attentive processing of humans. dashboards were UI-for-exploration: they helped humans spot patterns in data themselves. but if the agent is the one looking at the data now, the UI has to serve a different purpose: helping humans grok and verify the agent's reasoning, not explore the data themselves. so maybe UI-for-verification is the new thing? 

anyways we are in for a really exciting next few years

reviewedPosts.text:
LlamaParse is officially a verified connector on Claude! 🦙

Claude is perfectly fine for the occasional text-only PDF. But most of the context your agent needs lives in messy PDFs, spreadsheets, scanned forms, dense tables, and charts. 

Feeding those docs straight to the model burns through tokens and can lead to hallucinations when layouts get scrambled, chart values are missed, or numbers are pulled from the wrong column. 

LlamaParse converts those documents into clean, structured context Claude can work with. With the connector you can

✅️ Parse documents into clean Markdown, JSON, or HTML
✅️ Extract specific fields directly into your schema
✅️ Search across document collections with filesystem-style tools
✅️ Classify documents or split them into predefined sections

Live in the Claude Connectors Directory now !

https://t.co/MPWdk7g4l4
